chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Abdullah ibn Sa'id al-Askari narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Hamdan al-Qushayri informed us, saying: Al-Mughira ibn Muhammad ibn al-Muhlib informed us, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: Abdullah ibn Dawud narrated to me, from Fuzayl ibn Marzooq, from Atiyyah al-Awfi, from Abu Sa'id al-Khidri, who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said:

"I am leaving among you two things, one of which is longer than the other: The Book of Allah, a rope extended from the heaven to the earth, and my Itrat (Ahl al-Bayt). Indeed, they will not separate from each other until they meet me at the Pool (al-Kawthar)." I asked Abu Sa'id: "Who is his Itrat?" He replied: "The members of his household."

key_terms.أَهْلُ الْبَيْت: The People of the House, referring to the Prophet's family
key_terms.الْحَوْض: The Pool (of Kawthar) in Paradise where the Prophet will await his followers
key_terms.الْعِتْرَة: Offspring or family, specifically referring to the Ahl al-Bayt in this context
key_terms.حَبْلٌ مَمْدُود: A rope extended, metaphor for the Quran as a connecting link to God

ai.seo_question: What are the two things the Prophet left behind that will never separate?
ai.summary: This foundational Hadith al-Thaqalayn, recorded by Shaykh al-Saduq, establishes the inseparable bond between the Quran and the Ahl al-Bayt as dual, enduring sources of guidance for the Muslim Ummah. The metaphor of the Quran as a 'rope extended from heaven to earth' underscores its divine origin and stability, while the promise that the two will not separate until the Day of Judgment highlights the necessity of adhering to both to avoid misguidance. In Shia scholarship, this is often interpreted to mean that the Ahl al-Bayt serve as the living, authoritative interpreters of the Quranic text.
